column1: # DRAFT: FOR HUMAN REVIEW BEFORE SUBMITTING. Not submitted anywhere. QuickStatements V1: [-]Qid<TAB>Pnnn<TAB>+YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z/precision[<TAB>S143<TAB>Q328<TAB>S4656<TAB>"source url"]
# A line starting with "-" removes that statement; the next line adds the replacement, referenced as imported from English Wikipedia (S143 Q328) with the revision read (S4656).

# Wikidata values fetched live 2026-10-14 (wbgetentities); Wikipedia infobox "date" lines read 2026-10-14 at the revisions named. Remove all comment lines (starting with #) before pasting into QuickStatements.

# Context: these are the Wikidata dates behind the date_order_invalid / century-precision events in data/events.json (docs/data-fixes.md, "Checks of 2026-10-14"). middleeast.events never edits Wikidata; these are suggestions for the owner's own account.
# Iraqi invasion of Kuwait (Q856650): P580 start time 2009-08-02 (day) is after its own P582 1990-08-04; infobox "2–4 August 1990" (rev 1375300033). The year looks mistyped. Confidence: high.

# Second Battle of İnönü (Q2659746): P582 end time 1921-03-31 is before P585 1921-04-01; infobox "March 23 – April 1, 1921" (rev 1379641867) agrees with P585 for the end. Confidence: medium (P580 1921-03-26 vs the infobox's 23 March is a second disagreement; not suggested, the two sources differ).

# Israeli–Lebanese conflict (Q3241199): only date is P580 +2000-00-00 at century precision (Wikibase formats it "20. century", 1901–2000); infobox "15 May 1948 – present" (rev 1370624531). Confidence: high for the year; the infobox's start day is Wikipedia's choice of origin (1948 war).

# Arab Cold War (Q4783165): P585 point in time 1979-02-11 (day) sits on a period item that also has P580 1952 and P582 1970 (both year precision), and is after that end. The infobox says "23 July 1952 – 6 September 1991" with a note that sources variously end it c. 1979, 1990 or 1991 (rev 1380203502).

# NOT suggested as a statement: which end is right is a matter of sources, not a typo. A Wikidata editor could remove or deprecate the P585 (a point in time on a decades-long period) and give P582 the sourced alternatives; ask on the item's talk page first.

# Passover massacre (Q2660905): no error. P585 2002-03-27 (day) plus P580 and P582 "2002" (year precision); our pipeline used to read the year-precision end as 1 January 2002 and flag the event as reversed (fixed in scripts/lib/v21.js dateOrderFlags, 2026-10-14). Nothing to suggest.
# Added 2026-10-29 (Wikidata wbgetentities and the English articles read live that day, at the revisions named; docs/data-fixes.md, "Checks of 2026-10-29"):

# 2023 Afghanistan–Iran clash (Q118779713, revision 2459851515): P580 start time 2022-05-27 (day) is a year before the event; P585 is 2023-05 (month); infobox "27 May 2023" and lead "On 27 May 2023" (rev 1370424795). The year looks mistyped. Confidence: high.

# Battle of Gaza (2007) (Q373655, revision 2517661614): P580 start time 2007-06-10; infobox "7–15 June 2007" and lead "from 7 to 15 June 2007" (rev 1381695693); the infobox cites a PCHR report on the fighting of 7-14 June 2007. Confidence: medium (a source-based start, not a typo).

# Saudi–Yemeni war (1934) (Q1367731, revision 2538358965): P580 1934-03 (month), P582 1934-05-20 (day); infobox "20 March 1934 – 14 June 1934" (rev 1381123348). The start month agrees; the end differs by more than three weeks. NOT suggested: not traced which source either end follows.
